_meta.indication: Idursulfase (ELAPRASE) is indicated for patients with Hunter syndrome (Mucopolysaccharidosis II, MPS II); it has been shown to improve walking capacity in these patients.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: TKT024 (Phase II/III randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study)
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, international, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study comparing two idursulfase dosing regimens (weekly and every-other-week) versus placebo over 52 weeks, with 32 patients randomized to each of the three treatment groups at nine sites.
pivotal_trials.population: Male patients with MPS II (Hunter syndrome), ages 5 to 25 years, with I2S enzyme activity less than 10% of the lower limit of normal and normal activity of one other sulfatase; patients had to be able to stand six minutes for the walk test.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: A two-component composite score based on the sum of the ranks of the change from baseline to Week 53 in distance walked on the six-minute walk test (6MWT) and the ranks of the change in percent-predicted forced vital capacity (%FVC).
pivotal_trials.n: 96 patients (32 per arm: weekly, every-other-week, placebo)
pivotal_trials.result: The composite primary endpoint favored weekly idursulfase vs placebo (p=0.0049). The weekly group averaged a 35 meter greater adjusted mean increase in 6MWT distance vs placebo (p=0.01); the %FVC difference (4.28) was not statistically significant (p=0.0650).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=10% and more frequent than placebo) included pyrexia (63% vs 59%), headache (59% vs 44%), arthralgia (31% vs 28%), and pruritus (28% vs 16%). The most serious risk was infusion reactions: 16/108 patients (15%) experienced infusion reactions during 26 of 8,274 infusions (0.3%), including life-threatening anaphylactic reactions.
target_moa: Idursulfase is a recombinant form of the human lysosomal enzyme iduronate-2-sulfatase (I2S), which is deficient in MPS II; it provides an exogenous source of enzyme taken up into cellular lysosomes via mannose-6-phosphate receptors, where it hydrolyzes the glycosaminoglycans dermatan sulfate and heparan sulfate.
modality: Enzyme (recombinant human iduronate-2-sulfatase enzyme replacement therapy)

boxed_warning.content: Risk of anaphylaxis: life-threatening anaphylactic reactions have been observed during ELAPRASE infusions, so appropriate medical support should be readily available. Biphasic anaphylactic reactions have occurred and may require prolonged observation; patients with compromised respiratory function or acute respiratory disease may be at risk of serious acute exacerbation and require additional monitoring.

requirement.text: Evaluate long-term safety and efficacy data in an observational survey (Hunter Outcome Survey, HOS) of patients with Hunter syndrome treated with ELAPRASE, collecting data including the six-minute walk test and urinary GAG levels approximately every 6 to 12 months for at least 15 years.

citations.quote: Shire commits to evaluating long-term safety and efficacy data in an observational survey (the Hunter Outcome Survey, HOS) of patients with Hunter syndrome being treated with ELAPRASE.

the survey will collect data from patients on the six-minute walk test, from a subset of centers that will have the training and facilities to collect the data in a standardized and reproducible manner, and urinary GAG levels approximately every 6 to 12 months for at least 15 years.
